editorial:
Imagine meeting your best friends from elementary school after twenty long years. That is exactly what happens here, but it is far from a happy reunion. You follow three old pals who were split up during a wave of people leaving China. Now they are back in Hong Kong, but they have grown into completely different people. The vibe is heavy and moody, showing you a side of the city that feels tired and bored. As they try to reconnect, they all fall into messy, secret romances that they probably should have avoided. It is a slow burn that shows how old ties can either save you or pull you under.

What really works is how the movie handles the tension. The acting feels real, and the way the secrets slowly leak out keeps you interested even when the pace slows down. While some parts might feel a bit too sad or slow for people who want constant action, the emotional payoff is worth it. You should definitely check this out if you like stories about regret and lost time.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when the secret affairs and lies finally collide. The characters realize that their old friendship cannot fix the mistakes they made as adults. The story ends on a dark note, showing that betrayal leaves scars that never really heal. Instead of a happy ending, you are left with the sad reality that some people are too broken to ever truly go back to who they used to be.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about old friends and complicated relationships.
